title: Raft's commit rule and Figure 8
hook: Why can a Raft leader only commit entries from its own term by counting replicas?

scenes.caption: The leader appends client commands to its log and replicates them with AppendEntries.
scenes.narration: A client command goes to the leader, which appends it and sends AppendEntries. Once stored on a majority, it is committed and applied.

scenes.caption: Followers accept entries only if the previous entry matches, which keeps logs consistent.
scenes.narration: AppendEntries carries prevLogIndex and prevLogTerm. A follower rejects without a matching entry, and the leader backs up. This yields Log Matching.

elements.text:
AppendEntries(term, leaderId,
  prevLogIndex, prevLogTerm,
  entries[], leaderCommit)
Same index and term implies identical logs up to that index.

scenes.caption: Figure 8: an old-term entry on a majority can still be overwritten by a later leader.
scenes.narration: Figure 8: a term-2 entry reaches a majority, yet a server with a term-3 last entry can win an election and overwrite it.

items: S1 leads term 2, copies entry to S2
S1 crashes; S5 wins term 3, adds its own
S1 returns, re-replicates term-2 entry to S3
Majority has it, but S5 can still win

scenes.caption: So a leader commits only entries from its current term, by counting replicas.
scenes.narration: So a leader counts replicas to commit only entries from its own term. Committing one commits everything before it, through Log Matching.

elements.text:
for N > commitIndex:
  if log[N].term == currentTerm
  and majority matchIndex >= N:
    commitIndex = N

scenes.caption: Together with the election check, this guarantees committed entries survive every leadership change.
scenes.narration: With the election restriction, this gives Leader Completeness: committed entries are in every future leader's log. Many implementations append a no-op on election.

items: Commit only current-term entries by count
New leaders often append a no-op

takeaway: A Raft leader never counts replicas to commit an old-term entry; committing a current-term entry commits everything before it, closing the Figure 8 hole.
